statement: The function returns a result r and r is the maximum length of a contiguous substring of s in which every byte occurs at most twice. Equivalently: (a) for every i and j with 0 <= i <= j <= len(s), if for every byte value c the number of indices k with i <= k < j and s[k] = c is at most 2, then j - i <= r; and (b) there exist i and j with 0 <= i <= j <= len(s) such that j - i = r and for every byte value c the number of indices k with i <= k < j and s[k] = c is at most 2.
preconditions: len(s) is an integer with 2 <= len(s) <= 100, and for every k with 0 <= k < len(s), s[k] is an ASCII code of a lowercase English letter (97 <= s[k] <= 122).

statement: The function returns a result r; it does not panic, overflow, or access out of bounds.
preconditions: len(s) is an integer with 2 <= len(s) <= 100, and for every k with 0 <= k < len(s), s[k] is an ASCII code of a lowercase English letter (97 <= s[k] <= 122).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 2 <= r <= len(s).
preconditions: len(s) is an integer with 2 <= len(s) <= 100, and for every k with 0 <= k < len(s), s[k] is an ASCII code of a lowercase English letter (97 <= s[k] <= 122).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exist integers i and j such that 0 <= i <= j <= len(s), j - i = r, and for every byte value c the number of indices k with i <= k < j and s[k] = c is at most 2.
preconditions: len(s) is an integer with 2 <= len(s) <= 100, and for every k with 0 <= k < len(s), s[k] is an ASCII code of a lowercase English letter (97 <= s[k] <= 122).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i and j with 0 <= i <= j <= len(s), if for every byte value c the number of indices k with i <= k < j and s[k] = c is at most 2, then j - i <= r.
preconditions: len(s) is an integer with 2 <= len(s) <= 100, and for every k with 0 <= k < len(s), s[k] is an ASCII code of a lowercase English letter (97 <= s[k] <= 122).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = len(s) if and only if for every byte value c the number of indices k with 0 <= k < len(s) and s[k] = c is at most 2.
preconditions: len(s) is an integer with 2 <= len(s) <= 100, and for every k with 0 <= k < len(s), s[k] is an ASCII code of a lowercase English letter (97 <= s[k] <= 122).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if all entries of s are equal, that is, there exists a byte b such that s[k] = b for every k with 0 <= k < len(s), then r = 2.
preconditions: len(s) is an integer with 2 <= len(s) <= 100, and for every k with 0 <= k < len(s), s[k] is an ASCII code of a lowercase English letter (97 <= s[k] <= 122).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if there exists a byte value c such that the number of indices k with 0 <= k < len(s) and s[k] = c is at least 3, then r < len(s).
preconditions: len(s) is an integer with 2 <= len(s) <= 100, and for every k with 0 <= k < len(s), s[k] is an ASCII code of a lowercase English letter (97 <= s[k] <= 122).

statement: Let t be the byte slice of length len(s) defined by t[k] = s[len(s) - 1 - k] for every 0 <= k < len(s). If the function called on s returns r and the function called on t returns r_t, then r = r_t.
preconditions: len(s) is an integer with 2 <= len(s) <= 100, and for every k with 0 <= k < len(s), s[k] is an ASCII code of a lowercase English letter (97 <= s[k] <= 122).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if len(s) > 2 and r = 2, then all entries of s are equal.
preconditions: len(s) is an integer with 2 <= len(s) <= 100, and for every k with 0 <= k < len(s), s[k] is an ASCII code of a lowercase English letter (97 <= s[k] <= 122).

statement: Let t be any byte slice of length len(s) such that t also has length between 2 and 100, all entries of t are ASCII lowercase letters, and s and t have the same equality pattern: for all i and j with 0 <= i,j < len(s), s[i] = s[j] if and only if t[i] = t[j]. If the function called on s returns r_s and the function called on t returns r_t, then r_s = r_t.
preconditions: len(s) is an integer with 2 <= len(s) <= 100, and for every k with 0 <= k < len(s), s[k] is an ASCII code of a lowercase English letter (97 <= s[k] <= 122).

statement: Let D be the number of distinct byte values that occur among the entries of s. Whenever the function returns a result r, r <= 2 * D. In particular, since there are at most 26 distinct lowercase letters, r <= 52.
preconditions: len(s) is an integer with 2 <= len(s) <= 100, and for every k with 0 <= k < len(s), s[k] is an ASCII code of a lowercase English letter (97 <= s[k] <= 122).

statement: If the function called on s returns r_s and the function called on t returns r_t, then r_t <= r_s. Equivalently, taking a contiguous substring cannot increase the maximum admissible length.
preconditions: Let s satisfy: len(s) is an integer with 2 <= len(s) <= 100, and for every k with 0 <= k < len(s), s[k] is an ASCII code of a lowercase English letter (97 <= s[k] <= 122). Let i and j be integers with 0 <= i <= j <= len(s) and j - i >= 2, and let t be the slice defined by t[k] = s[i+k] for 0 <= k < j-i.
